title: Draft your first user story
why_matters: Three weeks in, you should have done enough listening to write a story that holds up. The first one is the hardest — not because writing is hard, but because committing to a specific framing in writing requires you to decide what you actually believe. After this, every story is easier.
steps: Pick one small piece of in-scope functionality on the current initiative. Smaller than you think you need.
Open the user-story playbook and draft the As-a / I want / So-that line. Then draft three Given-When-Then acceptance criteria — one happy path, one edge case, one security or boundary case.
Read it out loud. If it sounds like you're describing a feature rather than a behaviour, rewrite.
Send it to QA before sprint planning. Ask one specific question: which criterion will be hardest to test, and why?
success_criteria: One user story written with three acceptance criteria covering happy path / edge / boundary. QA has acknowledged it and named at least one concern.
reflection_prompt: What was the criterion you almost left out, and why did you almost leave it out?
